name: a flat engine-oil stain soaked into packed earth seen from above: a long diagonal smear with a small separate spot below it, dark core, soaked brown edge dithered into the dirt, one dull teal-grey sheen pixel
label: wasteland_ruins/oil-stain-b

refSet.reason: 칩셋 wasteland_ruins 의 화풍 기준 묶음이 없다

surfaces.part: packed earth ground patch with oil smears and a small spot

answer.evidence: The whole 64x48 sprite is a single flat, textured earth surface seen from above. Dark elongated stain cores sit at about rows 3-9, 19-26 and 36-42, with a teal-grey sheen pixel in each core and a grey/red speck cluster near rows 38-43. The column scans show only mottled brown earth, with no front-edge line, eave shadow, or vertical face. Every row is 64 wide, so there is no silhouette and no front face (0 rows). That is what a flat decal should look like, so it reads as a top-down slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a packed-earth ground patch with a dark oil smear and a small spot. It has about 5 visible tones per tile, against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so they carry a brown tint. There is no real outline; the stain is separated by value and dithering, which suits the brief. The soil has speckle and grain, but at this scale it looks fairly sparse and noisy, with few clustered pebbles or per-clump shading like the references. The stain core reads as only 2-3 steps (dark core, brown soak, dirt), which is shallower than the 5-6 step ramps in Beodeul. Raw distinct colours per tile are just 5, so density is a little below the references on its own terms. The piece is acceptable but does not clearly match the Beodeul craft level, and when in doubt it fails.
